clue.text: In retrospect he failed to win back his wife

definitions.text: In retrospect he failed to win back his wife

parts.words: In retrospect he failed to win back his wife
parts.note: the Greek musician who led his dead bride out of the underworld lost her by looking back, so 'in retrospect' is literal

explanation.surface: A man looks back on his failed attempt to save his marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth the lyre-player was allowed to lead Eurydice from Hades provided he did not look round; he did, and lost her.

clue.text: Short race requiring replacement of these stalls?

indicators.note: the letters of the two words have to be replaced in a new order

explanation.surface: A brief race means rearranging the seating stalls.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre the front seats on the ground floor are the orchestra stalls, called simply the orchestra in America.

clue.text: Brown first turned up on Rhode Island as Pilgrim Father probably

indicators.note: first says the other pieces come before the colour word in the answer
the little word up is turned over, so its letters run the other way

parts.note: taken as written
RI is the US postal abbreviation for Rhode Island
tan is a shade of brown

explanation.surface: A Mr Brown first appeared on Rhode Island, probably one of the founding settlers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means sitting above; 'first' says the colour word comes after the rest, though the surface reads it as Brown arriving first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pilgrim Fathers who sailed on the Mayflower were mostly strict Protestant dissenters of that sect.

clue.text: Cook's vessel, try to name it

definitions.meaning: Captain James Cook's ship on his first Pacific voyage
an attempt or effort, as a verb to strive

explanation.surface: Name Captain Cook's ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to name it' just asks the solver to supply the word.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Endeavour carried Cook to Australia; as a common word it means to strive or attempt.

clue.text: A feature in such windows as have ventilation

definitions.text: A feature in such windows as have ventilation

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Describing a part of windows that let in air.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the end of windows, all of as and the start of have; 'such windows' are the kind named by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sliding window frame that moves up and down in grooves is the defining part of a classic British window type.

clue.text: Tea vessel is put on this framework

parts.note: cha is informal British slang for tea
SS, steamship, stands for a vessel
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tea vessel is placed on a stand.
explanation.definitionFit: The base frame of a car or other vehicle, on which the body is mounted.

clue.text: "Improve on that' you said recently. Give up?

parts.note: to cap it is to go one better than something

indicators.note: said means the word you is heard, giving its sound-alike letter

parts.note: the pronoun sounds like the letter U
late means recently, as in 'of late'

explanation.surface: Someone challenged to better a remark is asked whether they surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: To capitulate is to surrender or yield.

clue.text: Deck that gives trouble to sailors

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: A ship's deck that causes problems for the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like the ship's floor but is the verb, to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something is to decorate or ornament it.

clue.text: Betting ring, right? Hurried to put this on Highland Laddie

parts.note: SP is the starting price in horse-race betting
a ring is shaped like the letter O
ran means hurried

explanation.surface: A bookmaker at the betting ring rushes to dress a Scottish boy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the pouch worn at the front of a Highlander's kilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scot in Highland dress wears a fur or leather pouch hung in front of his kilt.

clue.text: Strong competitor before end of play is out of sorts

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tennis draw

indicators.note: end of picks the closing letter of the word play

explanation.surface: A top player, just before the match finishes, feels unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling seedy is feeling slightly ill or below par.

clue.text: Bacon is this copper colour

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Bacon has a coppery colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bacon' might suggest the painter or philosopher; here it is just the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon is pork preserved by salting or smoking.

clue.text: In his second year US student hopes room will be changed

definitions.text: In his second year US student

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are to be altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An American college student hopes for a room change.
explanation.definitionFit: In American colleges and high schools, a second-year student has this title.

clue.text: Catch business associate losing ultimate right to retire

indicators.note: retire means go back, so the letters left are read backwards
the final letter of the associate is lost

parts.note: a partner is a business associate

explanation.surface: A firm's partner loses the last right to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing ultimate right' drops the final R of PARTNER, giving PARTNE; 'to retire' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To trap someone is to catch them out.

clue.text: Does this fish cause sun-burn?

parts.note: reading backwards along the compound, sun is a ray and burn is a sting, so the sea creature seems to cause it

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about whether a fish gives you sunburn.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat fish with a venomous barbed tail.

clue.text: Horse-dealer in turn is able to show the system Galileo followed

parts.note: coper is an old word for a horse-dealer

indicators.note: turn tells us the little word in goes round the other way

parts.note: taken as written
can means is able

explanation.surface: A horse-trader shows in turn that he understands Galileo's model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' looks like a phrase meaning 'in sequence' but turns IN into NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo supported the sun-centred cosmology named after the Polish astronomer who proposed it.

clue.text: In which dancers try to follow beat

indicators.note: to follow puts the attempt word after the beating word

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
a go is a try

explanation.surface: Dancers attempt to keep time with the beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance originating in Argentina, performed by couples.

clue.text: Slip into a new form of artistic media

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are given a fresh shape

explanation.surface: Moving into a new kind of artistic medium.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigments ground in linseed oil are a classic medium for painting on canvas.

clue.text: Movement and reform of nation

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: reform means the letters of nation are formed again in another order

explanation.surface: A political movement calling for national reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' is political in the surface but musical in fact; 'reform of' rearranges NATION into ANTINO.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece or section of music marked slightly faster than a walking pace.

clue.text: Discard the jalopy, fit only for this

definitions.text: Discard the jalopy, fit only for this

parts.words: Discard the jalopy, fit only for this
parts.note: an old banger of a car is only good for the pile of rubbish where unwanted things are thrown

explanation.surface: Get rid of the old car; it's fit only for the dump.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile of discarded metal, and figuratively the state of being useless.

clue.text: Missing, seen round the Globe soaking up the drink

indicators.note: round says the first word's letters enclose the second's

parts.note: absent means missing
an orb is a globe

explanation.surface: Missing, someone was seen around the Globe theatre, drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absorbent takes in liquid, like a sponge.

clue.text: Thus leading artist gets refusal from a singer

parts.note: so means thus
PRA is the President of the Royal Academy, Britain's leading artist
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A top artist is turned down by a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest female singing voice, and a singer with it.

clue.text: Artist shows doctor holding flower

indicators.note: holding means the doctor letters wrap round the river

parts.note: flower in crosswords is something that flows, a river; the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: An artist depicts a doctor holding a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means 'one that flows', a river: the Ure in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was the great German Renaissance painter and engraver.

clue.text: What spinners did to trade perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of to trade could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: What spinning-mill workers did for their trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that spin have turned round an axis.

clue.text: Coming down to the point, record call

parts.note: to tape is to record
to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: Getting to the point, a phone call is recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: Something narrowing towards a tip gradually thins to a point.

clue.text: On which the matter for discussion is supporting the water supply

definitions.text: On which the matter for discussion

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue puts the little word beneath the other

parts.note: a tap supplies water
taken as written

explanation.surface: The agenda item is backing the water supply.
explanation.walkthrough: A matter under discussion is 'on the tapis', from the old table-cloth of a council table.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapis is a tablecloth or covering; a subject under consideration is said to be on it.

clue.text: Sternly rebuked a troop-leader getting overdrawn

indicators.note: getting here means the red letters take in the others

parts.note: an overdrawn account is in the red
taken as written

indicators.note: leader picks the opening letter of troop

explanation.surface: A troop commander is told off for being overdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone is an old use meaning to scold them angrily.

clue.text: How, troops march in a word, being part of the foot

definitions.text: How, troops march in a word
definitions.meaning: soldiers march keeping in time together
the arched middle section of the foot

explanation.surface: Soldiers march together; also a part of the foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a word' asks for the two-word phrase run together as one.
explanation.definitionFit: Marching in time is keeping in step; the arched upper middle of the foot has this name.

clue.text: Sad expression of a girl failing to finish

indicators.note: the girl word does not reach its last letter

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl fails to finish, an occasion for sadness.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of grief or regret.

clue.text: But this examination is no such joke

definitions.text: But this examination is no such joke

parts.words: But this examination is no such joke
parts.note: the same adjective describes a hands-on test and a prank played on someone

explanation.surface: This test is no laughing matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hands-on test in science is a practical; a prank is a practical joke.

clue.text: Man for instance comprehends the origin of this fibre

indicators.note: comprehends in its old sense of contains, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an example of an island

indicators.note: the origin of picks the opening letter of this

explanation.surface: A man understands where this fibre comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a plant fibre from agave or yucca, used for cord and brushes.

clue.text: Mountain said to be not without falls' in' winter

indicators.note: said to be means we hear a phrase that sounds like the answer

parts.note: with snow coming down, a winter landscape is not without falls of snow

explanation.surface: A mountain is described as having snowfalls in winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls' are snowfalls, not waterfalls; Snowdon is the highest mountain in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest mountain in Wales.

clue.text: Rose left in the lurch

definitions.meaning: abandoned, especially failing to keep a date

explanation.surface: Getting up and deserting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who got to their feet did this; a date who never turns up has done it to you.
